title: Held back response
summary: A response document whose file modification time is well before its release, released close to the statutory deadline.

sections.heading: What it flags
paragraphs: A response document whose file modification time is well before its release, released close to the statutory deadline. This suggests the response was ready earlier.

sections.heading: What it does not show
paragraphs: That the deadline was missed. It was met. This is a pattern about timing and intent, not a violation.

sections.heading: How it is labelled
paragraphs: Basis: Pattern signal, not a legal claim. Confidence is shown only when it was measured, and reads Unassessed otherwise.

title: Boilerplate denial
summary: Near-identical denial wording reused across unrelated requests within one agency, which can indicate stock refusals instead of individual review.

sections.heading: What it flags
paragraphs: Near-identical denial wording reused across unrelated requests within one agency, which can indicate stock refusals instead of individual review.

sections.heading: What it does not show
paragraphs: That any denial was improper. Reusing wording is a pattern, and the legal basis of each denial is not evaluated.

sections.heading: How it is labelled
paragraphs: Basis: Pattern signal, not a legal claim. Confidence is shown only when it was measured, and reads Unassessed otherwise.

title: Just-in-time compliance
summary: An agency whose closures cluster in the last day before the statutory deadline at a rate materially above the population base rate.

sections.heading: What it flags
paragraphs: An agency whose closures cluster in the last day before the statutory deadline at a rate materially above the population base rate.

sections.heading: What it does not show
paragraphs: A violation. Every closure counted was within the deadline. It is a behavioral pattern.

sections.heading: How it is labelled
paragraphs: Basis: Pattern signal, not a legal claim. Confidence is shown only when it was measured, and reads Unassessed otherwise.

title: Extension pattern
summary: One statutory extension reason accounts for the overwhelming majority of an agency's invoked extensions.

sections.heading: What it flags
paragraphs: One statutory extension reason accounts for the overwhelming majority of an agency's invoked extensions.

sections.heading: What it does not show
paragraphs: That any single extension was invalid. A valid extension is legitimate. Only the reliance on one ground is flagged.

sections.heading: How it is labelled
paragraphs: Basis: Pattern signal, not a legal claim. Confidence is shown only when it was measured, and reads Unassessed otherwise.

title: Gap in a numbered sequence
summary: A released set with self-labelled sequential numbers (invoices, memos, resolutions) whose numeric span exceeds what was released, with numbers missing from a tight sequence.

sections.heading: What it flags
paragraphs: A released set with self-labelled sequential numbers (invoices, memos, resolutions) whose numeric span exceeds what was released, with numbers missing from a tight sequence.

sections.heading: What it does not show
paragraphs: That records were withheld. Numbers can be skipped for ordinary reasons. It is a lead to ask about.

sections.heading: How it is labelled
paragraphs: Basis: Pattern signal, not a legal claim. Confidence is shown only when it was measured, and reads Unassessed otherwise.

title: Differential treatment
summary: Outcomes for requests attributed to one requester class that differ materially from the agency's own baseline: denial rate, latency or redaction density.

sections.heading: What it flags
paragraphs: Outcomes for requests attributed to one requester class that differ materially from the agency's own baseline: denial rate, latency or redaction density.

sections.heading: What it does not show
paragraphs: Discrimination or a legal violation. Without a per-request statutory finding it is a statistical pattern.

sections.heading: How it is labelled
paragraphs: Basis: Pattern signal, not a legal claim. Confidence is shown only when it was measured, and reads Unassessed otherwise.

title: Metadata contradicts content
summary: A document whose own metadata disagrees with its content, such as text citing events after its declared creation time, or a document marked Final that cites a later draft.

sections.heading: What it flags
paragraphs: A document whose own metadata disagrees with its content, such as text citing events after its declared creation time, or a document marked Final that cites a later draft.

sections.heading: What it does not show
paragraphs: Who changed the document or why. It is a pattern consistent with backdating or silent modification, and has innocent explanations too.

sections.heading: How it is labelled
paragraphs: Basis: Pattern signal, not a legal claim. Confidence is shown only when it was measured, and reads Unassessed otherwise.

title: Regenerated response
summary: A response whose file metadata predates its release by weeks or months, with the metadata fields consistent with each other.

sections.heading: What it flags
paragraphs: A response whose file metadata predates its release by weeks or months, with the metadata fields consistent with each other. It does not require release near a deadline.

sections.heading: What it does not show
paragraphs: That the response was intentionally delayed. Files are often edited or re-saved for unrelated reasons.

sections.heading: How it is labelled
paragraphs: Basis: Pattern signal, not a legal claim. Confidence is shown only when it was measured, and reads Unassessed otherwise.

title: Email thread gap
summary: A released .msg message that refers, through its reply headers, to a message that is not in the released set.

sections.heading: What it flags
paragraphs: A released .msg message that refers, through its reply headers, to a message that is not in the released set.

sections.heading: What it does not show
paragraphs: What the missing message says, or that it is responsive. The released set is simply not the whole exchange.

sections.heading: How it is labelled
paragraphs: Basis: Pattern signal, not a legal claim. Confidence is shown only when it was measured, and reads Unassessed otherwise.

title: Contradictory statements
summary: Two documents in the collection that assert the same subject and predicate with materially different values, for example a 3-year and a 7-year retention period.

sections.heading: What it flags
paragraphs: Two documents in the collection that assert the same subject and predicate with materially different values, for example a 3-year and a 7-year retention period.

sections.heading: What it does not show
paragraphs: Which statement is right, or that either is binding. It is an internal-consistency pattern.

sections.heading: How it is labelled
paragraphs: Basis: Pattern signal, not a legal claim. Confidence is shown only when it was measured, and reads Unassessed otherwise.

title: No-records denial contradicted by other releases
summary: A response saying no responsive records exist, while at least three other public documents released to different requesters mention the same topic.

sections.heading: What it flags
paragraphs: A response saying no responsive records exist, while at least three other public documents released to different requesters mention the same topic.

sections.heading: What it does not show
paragraphs: That the denial was wrong. Scope and legal treatment differ, and the detector does not evaluate them.

sections.heading: How it is labelled
paragraphs: Basis: Pattern signal, not a legal claim. Confidence is shown only when it was measured, and reads Unassessed otherwise.

title: Paraphrased denials
summary: Denial language that is highly similar in vocabulary across distinct requests but has different surface phrasing, which would defeat a direct boilerplate match.

sections.heading: What it flags
paragraphs: Denial language that is highly similar in vocabulary across distinct requests but has different surface phrasing, which would defeat a direct boilerplate match.

sections.heading: What it does not show
paragraphs: Intent to evade. It is a pattern in wording and is not a legal claim.

sections.heading: How it is labelled
paragraphs: Basis: Pattern signal, not a legal claim. Confidence is shown only when it was measured, and reads Unassessed otherwise.

title: Releases just under round numbers
summary: An agency's released-document counts cluster just below a round number such as 10, 25, 50, 100, 500 or 1,000, with few or none above it.

sections.heading: What it flags
paragraphs: An agency's released-document counts cluster just below a round number such as 10, 25, 50, 100, 500 or 1,000, with few or none above it.

sections.heading: What it does not show
paragraphs: That releases were sized on purpose. Round-number clustering can have ordinary causes.

sections.heading: How it is labelled
paragraphs: Basis: Pattern signal, not a legal claim. Confidence is shown only when it was measured, and reads Unassessed otherwise.

title: Redaction with no residual signals
summary: Heavily redacted documents that show almost no structural residual signals across a meaningful sample.

sections.heading: What it flags
paragraphs: Heavily redacted documents that show almost no structural residual signals across a meaningful sample. Either exemplary redaction practice, or redactions tuned to what the residual audit can see.

sections.heading: What it does not show
paragraphs: Wrongdoing. Clean redaction is also what good practice looks like.

sections.heading: How it is labelled
paragraphs: Basis: Pattern signal, not a legal claim. Confidence is shown only when it was measured, and reads Unassessed otherwise.

title: Records released after a no-records denial
summary: A no-responsive-records denial followed by public releases from the same agency, dated after the determination, that match the denied request's topic vocabulary.

sections.heading: What it flags
paragraphs: A no-responsive-records denial followed by public releases from the same agency, dated after the determination, that match the denied request's topic vocabulary.

sections.heading: What it does not show
paragraphs: That the records were responsive to that request, or that the denial was in bad faith.

sections.heading: How it is labelled
paragraphs: Basis: Pattern signal, not a legal claim. Confidence is shown only when it was measured, and reads Unassessed otherwise.

title: Inferred redaction candidate
summary: A redaction with a likely candidate identity derived from surrounding context and at least three independent corroborating documents.

sections.heading: What it flags
paragraphs: A redaction with a likely candidate identity derived from surrounding context and at least three independent corroborating documents.

sections.heading: What it does not show
paragraphs: That the redacted identity is known. It is inference, not decryption, and is tagged as a hypothesis wherever it appears. Verifiable reports leave it out.

sections.heading: How it is labelled
paragraphs: Basis: Pattern signal, not a legal claim. Confidence is shown only when it was measured, and reads Unassessed otherwise.

title: Shared language across agencies
summary: The same denial paragraph appearing across multiple agencies, which can point to a shared template or circulating guidance.

sections.heading: What it flags
paragraphs: The same denial paragraph appearing across multiple agencies, which can point to a shared template or circulating guidance.

sections.heading: What it does not show
paragraphs: Coordination. Shared wording can come from a public template or standard legal text.

sections.heading: How it is labelled
paragraphs: Basis: Pattern signal, not a legal claim. Confidence is shown only when it was measured, and reads Unassessed otherwise.

title: Change in agency behavior
summary: One agency's behavior stepping over a date: a large jump in heavy-redaction rate, or determination latency roughly doubling, found by a bounded change-point scan with minimum data on both sides.

sections.heading: What it flags
paragraphs: One agency's behavior stepping over a date: a large jump in heavy-redaction rate, or determination latency roughly doubling, found by a bounded change-point scan with minimum data on both sides.

sections.heading: What it does not show
paragraphs: Why the change happened. It marks when, not why.

sections.heading: How it is labelled
paragraphs: Basis: Pattern signal, not a legal claim. Confidence is shown only when it was measured, and reads Unassessed otherwise.

title: Orphan topic
summary: A topic prominent in one agency's records and entirely absent from another agency's records in the same jurisdiction, when the second agency has enough requests to trust the absence.

sections.heading: What it flags
paragraphs: A topic prominent in one agency's records and entirely absent from another agency's records in the same jurisdiction, when the second agency has enough requests to trust the absence.

sections.heading: What it does not show
paragraphs: That records are missing. Agencies have different functions.

sections.heading: How it is labelled
paragraphs: Basis: Pattern signal, not a legal claim. Confidence is shown only when it was measured, and reads Unassessed otherwise.

title: Reused extension ground
summary: One statutory extension reason invoked across topically diverse requests, on top of the concentration test, which suggests a catch-all rationale.

sections.heading: What it flags
paragraphs: One statutory extension reason invoked across topically diverse requests, on top of the concentration test, which suggests a catch-all rationale.

sections.heading: What it does not show
paragraphs: That any extension was improper. It is a pattern signal.

sections.heading: How it is labelled
paragraphs: Basis: Pattern signal, not a legal claim. Confidence is shown only when it was measured, and reads Unassessed otherwise.

title: Agency exceeded its own stated commitment
summary: A counted comparison: a calendar-day response time that the agency's own policy document states, against how long requests to that agency in the same portal actually took after the policy took effect.

sections.heading: What it flags
paragraphs: A counted comparison: a calendar-day response time that the agency's own policy document states, against how long requests to that agency in the same portal actually took after the policy took effect. Only a sourced determination event measures the period. Requests with a recorded statutory extension are excluded, and the policy applies only to the agency that issued it.

sections.heading: What it does not show
paragraphs: A court finding. It is the one finding kind labelled Legal claim: counted violation, and it is a count against the agency's own words. When the policy states no effective date, the upload time is used, the finding says so, and confidence is lower.

sections.heading: How it is labelled
paragraphs: Basis: Legal claim: counted violation. Confidence is derived from what the evaluation observed.

title: Claim contradicts data
summary: A quantitative statement in a released document, such as a total or a change, that falls outside the rounding band its own wording carries when checked against the imported budget or actuals table for the same fiscal year, fund and jurisdiction.

sections.heading: What it flags
paragraphs: A quantitative statement in a released document, such as a total or a change, that falls outside the rounding band its own wording carries when checked against the imported budget or actuals table for the same fiscal year, fund and jurisdiction.

sections.heading: What it does not show
paragraphs: Which side is right. It compares a sentence with a dataset. It only runs when a budget or actuals table has been imported, and unreconciled claims are not reported as contradictions.

sections.heading: How it is labelled
paragraphs: Basis: Pattern signal, not a legal claim. Confidence is shown only when it was measured, and reads Unassessed otherwise.

title: Correlated findings
summary: Two or more findings of different kinds that name exactly the same document, request or agency.

sections.heading: What it flags
paragraphs: Separate detectors that each flagged the same document, request or agency. Only an exact subject match counts; a document finding is never attributed to its agency by inference.

sections.heading: What it does not show
paragraphs: That the signals share a cause. Each member keeps its own basis and stays in the inbox; a legal-claim member is not made stronger by appearing here.

sections.heading: How it is labelled
paragraphs: Basis: Pattern signal, not a legal claim. Confidence is the weakest member's, and reads Unassessed when any member is unassessed.
